neighbours.label: Unclear: weak activity at the end of a normative or evaluative clause in argumentative prose (period, semicolon or the evaluative word itself)
fire: Health care is a public duty. Hospitals should not turn away people who cannot pay.
In my view the tax is regressive; consequently, poorer households carry most of the burden.
Only rich districts could hire extra teachers, and that made the whole scheme unjust.
The council is responsible for the roads. Drivers should not have to fix potholes themselves.
Diese Pflicht betrifft allerdings nur private Anbieter. Öffentliche Stellen sind davon ausgenommen.
Banning the drug outright would be unwise, because patients would simply buy it elsewhere.
The policy is cruel and short-sighted. It punishes the people it claims to protect.
I have no stake in either of the parties discussed below. I simply describe what they propose.
quiet: The bus left the depot at seven. It reached the village an hour later.
We packed sandwiches, apples and a flask of tea for the trip.
My cousin moved to Leeds in March and found a flat near the station.
The train stopped twice before it reached the coast that evening.
Am Morgen fuhren wir mit dem Rad zum See und badeten.
He opened the box, took out the lamp and plugged it into the wall.
The children built a sandcastle and then went for ice cream.
Grandma knitted a red scarf and sent it to me by post.

predictions: Weak; most fire items 0.15-0.30, plain narrative near misses below 0.10. Expected to fail the median.
notes: Card peaks on '.' and ';' closing claims in opinion/argument prose (Arabic, German, English). Probe: argumentative clause ends 0.17-0.27 ('which made the system unfair' 0.265, 'body weight;' 0.211, German 'jedoch' 0.217), but a cheerful narrative clause 'The weather was nice' also 0.245 and the plain 'The meeting ended at noon.' 0.034. Nothing reached 0.30, so this is registered as unclear.
